codeReview.summary: Realtime policy filtering and session-start enforcement are implemented with good test coverage, but the new validator introduces a policy regression for xAI/custom realtime starts when model is omitted.

issues.description: validateRealtimeModelAccess rejects restricted users when session.start omits model because it checks allowed.has(model) with model undefined, but the realtime flow still supports omitted models for xAI/custom providers (broker does not require model for non-OpenAI/Azure/Google and resolveXAISessionConfig falls back to DEFAULT_XAI_REALTIME_MODELS[0]). This blocks valid restricted-user xAI sessions unless clients always send an explicit model. Evidence: broker.js:97 calls validation before provider resolution; modelService.js:599 applies xAI default model fallback; modelService.js:690 throws on missing match.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The backend-migration-worker skill does not explicitly warn that full api suite runs can timeout on this host, even though workers repeatedly rely on targeted patterns to complete backend validation reliably.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Handoff skillFeedback.suggestedChanges in 2026-04-05T12-47-39-541Z__preserve-code-interpreter-and-realtime-workflows__4be56d70-d828-4fc4-b24d-52291fc3f8d4.json requests adding this guidance.

summary: Feature preserves most realtime/code-interpreter behavior and adds server-side realtime policy filtering/enforcement, but it regresses restricted-user xAI/custom session-starts when model is omitted; review marked fail pending that fix.
